title: Does BucketBy clause while writing Pyspark dataframe shuflle the data
question:
I am writing a pyspark dataframe as table in my Spark warehouse. I am bucketing it on specific column using bucketBy clause and assigning 10 buckets. I have read on several blog posts that bucketBy shuffle the data across partitions and assign key based on hash(key) % num_buckets. Upon seeing the execution plan, I can't see any shuffle stage. I can see the initial dataframe is being read in 12 partitions(df.rdd.numPartitions). Here is code.

(
    commodity_df
        .write
        .format("parquet")
        .bucketBy(10,"State")
        .sortBy("State")
        .saveAsTable("taxidb.commodityTbl")
)

Please find the screeshots of spark configuration, explain plan and details link.

Kindly excuse my ignorance and let me know where is the gap in my understanding.
answer:
After I did some trial locally what I found is in spark bucketby does not need shuffle as it creates as many bucket files as there are partitions. i.e if bucket value is 10 and partition is 12 then it creates 10 bucket files for every partition i.e 10*12 = 120 files so it does not need a shuffle.
File marked as first bucket xxx_0001_xxx you will see 12 of those in your table directory.
For ex: My directory had this kind of partitioned parquet files . part-00008-e5c66cf8-b641-48b9-b4ff-617f36f01209_00001.c000.snappy with 12 files containing this part 617f36f01209_00001 which indicates a bucket. Similarly 12 of xxx_0002_xxx and so on until bucket 10. When you join two such bucketed tables it will read all the files of bucket xxx_0001_xxx within one partition as to ensure no shuffle again.
The behaviour you expected seem to be only in Apache hive while spark does this optimisation where the no.of files increases but there is no shuffle. Hope this helps.
